set.body:
Problem: no test proves that a printed formula or a portable build spec rebuilds the same design. FormulaPrinterSuite.scala:6-21 checks parse(print(f)) == f on five generic formulas; FormulaGrammarSuite builds from formula.text but never compares with the original build; ModelBuildSpecJsonCodecSuite.scala:9-24 checks spec equality only. The printer ticket bd-01M3YZT25ZC3R3V0CESB7RQ9DJ asked for the five example studies and closed without them. The refusal of per-event peak scales with basis orthogonalization (ConvolvedBasisOrthogonalization.scala:40) is enforced but untested.

Consumer need: the studio's formula drawer is a second view of the same model (spec invariant I1, section 6).

Acceptance:
- A corpus covering the five studio studies (block, mixed gambles with modulators, delayed match-to-sample phases, stop-signal FIR, 12-cell x 3-basis factorial), LSA and LSS, and each modulator n/a policy.
- For each: build(original) and build(parse(print)) and build(decode(encode(ModelBuildSpec))) agree on column ids, design fingerprint and values within 1e-12, on JVM and JS.
- A negative test pins the per-event-peak/orthogonalization refusal message.

Out of scope: new grammar.
Provenance: verified read-only 2026-10-08 against ScalaFIM main ea6fe3ad for the PLS Neuro model studio (plsneuro review bd-01M4DMGP1QFSQX9Z5V91B4B12F; spec docs/plans/2026-10-02-model-studio-spec.md and GRAMMAR-NEEDS.md on plsneuro main).
set.title: Prove printed formulas and portable build specs rebuild identical designs
